_comment: Per-map correction between the game's RAM coordinates and the map image's
tile grid:  imageTile = (ram_x - dx, ram_y - dy).
Most maps need no entry - a vgmaps rip of a route or town starts at the
game's (0,0), so RAM coordinates index the image directly. Some interior
rips are cropped tighter than the real map, usually losing a wall row or
column, and every RAM-derived tile on them is then shifted by that much.
Template matching catches this on big maps (locationTracker warns when a
confident match disagrees with RAM), but interiors are smaller than the
240x160 screen and can't be matched at all, so their offsets have to be
measured. Stand on a tile you can point to in the map image and run:
PewterCity-Gym: the rip is missing its left wall column - note that col 11
is solid wall in every row while col 0 is walkable floor. Entering the gym
puts you on the door, which the image shows at col 5, but RAM reports x=6.
